articles.title: 'This is my final word, celebration of her', says Diana's brother
articles.summary: "This is my swan song too. I'm not here to bang on about Diana, this is my final word, celebration of her", Earl Spencer told presenter Laura Kuenssberg.
articles.body:
Earl Spencer, brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, said he misses his sister every day during an interview with the BBC.

"That's the thing with sibling loss, you never get over it," he told Laura Kuenssberg.

His book, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, is due to be published on Tuesday and is expected to be highly critical of the Royal Family.

He said one of the reasons the book is called Swan Song is because it is his "sign off" as Diana's brother and "final take on the situation".

"This is my swan song too. I'm not here to bang on about Diana, this is my final word, celebration of her," he added.

The full interview, Princess Diana: My Sister's Story, is available on BBC iPlayer and will be broadcast on BBC One at 18:30 BST on Sunday.

articles.title: Earl Spencer says he felt Charles had 'giddy tone' during call after Diana's death
articles.summary: Princess Diana's brother has been interviewed by the BBC ahead of the release of his book on the late Princess of Wales.
articles.body:
Earl Spencer has said he felt there was a "lightness" in the tone of the then-Prince Charles during a phone call following the death of his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales.

In an interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, he said he took a call at his home in Cape Town from Charles, who told him how he had broken the news to Princes William and Harry at Balmoral Castle.

"I felt there was a sort of giddy tone," Earl Spencer told the BBC. "I'd had a lot of calls that day from people who cared, who were stunned... and I just felt there was a lightness in his tone about Diana's death that really jarred with me."

Buckingham Palace released a rare statement on Wednesday in response to claims made by Earl Spencer in his book Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, which is due to be published on Tuesday.

It said the King was "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss".

The full interview, Princess Diana: My Sister's Story, is available on BBC iPlayer and will be broadcast on BBC One at 18:30 BST on Sunday.

articles.title: Diana’s brother says Harry and Meghan face 'cancerous' press
articles.summary: Earl Spencer says that he can see echoes of Princess Diana's treatment from the press in the way Harry and Meghan are scrutinised.
articles.body:
Earl Spencer has told the BBC that there are similarities between the way his sister Diana, Princess of Wales and the Duke and Duchess of Sussex have been treated by the press.

He said Princess Diana was "brought low" by press criticism of her and that it is a "pity" to see echoes of that in Harry and Meghan's lives now.

He added that people should learn from Princess Diana's example, and that for anyone being "destroyed daily" by the tabloid press, it must be a "cancerous influence" on their lives.

The full interview with Laura Kuenssberg, Princess Diana: My Sister's Story, will be available on iPlayer from 16:00 and broadcast on BBC One at 18:30 BST on Sunday.

articles.title: What's the future look like for the PGA Tour's new event in North Carolina?
articles.summary: The Biltmore Championship is Asheville's first PGA Tour event in 84 years, aiding recovery after Hurricane Helene.
articles.body:
ASHEVILLE, N.C. - With the Blue Ridge Mountains framing the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship Asheville , an event now in full swing at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove in Arden, many spectators were seeing a PGA Tour event live for the first time.

Off the green, the audience politely applauded the players in the tournament that began with nearly 130 competitors.

Griffin Collins, an Atlanta resident, said he had attended PGA Tour events before that and said the Biltmore Championship Asheville stands up to the best of them.

"It's super cool. The course is beautiful," he said.

Collins attended the Biltmore Championship Asheville with friends the day before his wedding in the city. It was a bonus for the golf fan, as the wedding was planned before the PGA Tour was announced.

It's the first PGA Tour event in Asheville in 84 years, hosted on the Jack Nicklaus-designed course at a venue more than 23,000 square feet, which opened in 2005.

"It is a beautiful day to showcase Asheville and Western North Carolina to the entire golfing world," Governor Josh Stein said on the second morning of the tournament. "It's going to show these gorgeous mountains to viewers all over the world, and people are going to say to themselves, 'I want to go there,' and that's what we want to do ― let the world know Western North Carolina is open for business."

Western North Carolina shines for Biltmore Championship Asheville

Without a fog delay, as on the first day of the prestigious tournament, the professional men's golfers began the second day of the inaugural tournament under clear skies and sunshine, playing their way around the course and moving closer to claiming the victory, the custom-made gold-and-silver trophy and a cut of the $5 million purse.

The Biltmore Championship Asheville is the first of eight in the FedEx Fall Series, played after the Tour Championship, which finalizes eligibility for the 2027 PGA Tour Season.

Collins was rooting for the Vanderbilt University alum Gordon Sargent.

"Hopefully he can get back in the league and get back up there," he said.

Before Stein made his rounds of the holes, he paused to comment on the players with local ties.

"It's great that some of the most talented golfers in the world are North Carolinians. We have J.T. Polston and Webb Simpson competing here, and we're cheering hard for them," he said.

Post-Helene economy, recovery boost in WNC

The Biltmore Championship Asheville was secured through a $2.4 million four-year agreement between the PGA Tour and co-sponsors Biltmore, of the famed Biltmore Estate and Biltmore House, and Explore Asheville.

More than 10,000 guests were expected to attend the sold-out four-day event, with more than 2,000 out-of-state visitors, according to Explore Asheville. More than 1,100 volunteers registered to help before and during the tournament.

Anna Catherine, a Hickory resident and staff member at the University of North Carolina Asheville, signed up to volunteer three days over the weekend.

"It's a great way to get out and meet people and give back, which is one of the core pillars of what we do for the community, and I wanted to do my part," she said. "I wanted to be part of what makes it special and bringing people back to Asheville."

The future of Biltmore Championship Asheville, WNC

Stein said the PGA Tour is expected to significantly boost the region's economy, generating millions of dollars over the four-day weekend, accelerating WNC's recovery progress since Hurricane Helene, which arrived as a tropical storm in the fall of 2024.

Collins said he and his fiancée had visited Asheville many times before and after Helene, ultimately choosing an undisclosed venue in the city to exchange vows and celebrate.

"Our venue was under five feet of water but they rebuilt everything, so we felt good with going there since they were back up and running," he said.

During the four-day visit, he, his wedding party, and guests planned to venture outside The Cliffs at Walnut Cove to local businesses, including a welcome party at Hi-Wire Brewing, with food catered by Bear's Smokehouse BBQ , also a PGA Tour food vendor.

Collins said he planned to return for the next years of the Biltmore Championship Asheville.

Stein said the Biltmore Championship Asheville aims to accelerate the region's recovery, adding that there have been "encouraging indicators" of taxable sales in 2026, compared to before the historic storm.

"We see progress being made, but we know there's a lot more work to do," Stein said.

He said employment in Buncombe County hadn't fully rebounded , but that the way to boost employment is to increase local money circulation.

Asheville's unemployment rate was 3.3% in July 2026, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

"We want the world to know what we know about Western North Carolina. It's so beautiful; the people are nice, they're friendly, they're kind. The food is great, the beer is good, the crafts are beautiful. There's just so much to enjoy in Western North Carolina; we want more people to come here and spend their money."

Tiana Kennell is the food and dining reporter for the Asheville Citizen Times, part of USA TODAY Co., covering the food and beverage industry and PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship Asheville. articles.title: Manuel Elvira colidera el BMW PGA Championship con Alejandro del Rey a un golpe
articles.standfirst: Los españoles, de lleno en la pelea por ganar en Wentworth frente a los Spaun, Niemann, McIlroy, Aberg...
articles.summary: Los españoles, de lleno en la pelea por ganar en Wentworth frente a los Spaun, Niemann, McIlroy, Aberg...
articles.body: La actuación de los jugadores españoles en la tercera ronda del BMW PGA Championship fue extraordinaria, hasta el punto de que dos miembros de la ‘Armada’ están de lleno en la pelea por el torneo más prestigioso de la temporada regular del DP World Tour. Manuel Elvira es colíder en Wentworth, la casa del Circuito Europeo, junto al italiano Filippo Celli, ambos muy consistentes esta semana. Este domingo volverán a compartir partido, pero esta vez será en el ‘estelar’. El cántabro, que buscará estrenar su palmarés profesional mañana, firmó unos segundos nueve hoyos muy buenos, logrando un birdie de mérito en el 12 y un par complicado en el 13. "Creo que estoy listo [para ganar], he estado jugando bien las últimas semanas. Obviamente, los resultados no me acompañaban, pero esta semana logré mantener la calma y simplemente disfrutar", apuntó Manuel tras finalizar la ronda. El día del movimiento en el mítico recorrido de Surrey fue precioso, con Alejandro del Rey (ocho birdies sin bogeys) y el estadounidense Johannes Veerman (204) firmando la mejor vuelta del día (64 golpes) para subir como la espuma en la clasificación y situarse a un golpe de la cabeza. El madrileño, un jugador que cuando está inspirado bate récords, vuela por debajo del radar esta semana entre tanto gallo, pero su candidatura para el triunfo es firme. Junto a ellos, con 204 golpes, JJ Spaun, todo un ganador del US Open (2025) que este año ya levantó el Texas Open. También hizo 64 el noruego Kristoffer Reitan, otro ganador este año en el PGA Tour y y entre los convocados por Luke Donald para acudir a la concentración de Adare Manor -sede de la Ryder Cup 2027- de hace unos días. Reitan está en el grupo de 205 golpes en el que también se encuentran Rory McIlroy, Joaquín Niemann, Adam Scott, Ryan Fox, Ludvig Aberg, Bob MacIntyre o Matt Wallace. Imposible pedir más nivel al torneo. La nómina de estrellas bien posicionadas no acaba ahí y tampoco hay que olvidar al español Nacho Elvira, uno de los jugadores más regulares del circuito este año, que con 208 en el acumulado mantiene posibilidades de victoria o, cuanto menos, de anotarse un ‘top 10’ que lo consolidaría en la pelea por las tarjetas del PGA Tour. Eugenio López-Chacarra, con 209, también aspira a un gran resultado, así como Ángel Ayora (210). La ‘Armada’ está que sale en uno de los torneos de más nivel del DPWT. David Puig y Rafa Cabrera (212) también están completando una semana muy positiva.

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship 2026: Rory McIlroy two off pace as Manuel Elvira and Filippo Celli share third-round lead at Wentworth
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy among group of 20 players who will go into final round of BMW PGA Championship within four shots of the lead; watch final round live on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday
articles.body:
Rather remarkably, 20 players will go into Sunday within four shots of the lead, including Rory McIlroy, who produced a box-office finish, sending the patrons into delirium on the 18th by making an eagle to move within two shots of the pace-setting duo at 11 under par.

McIlroy equalled four other players - Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan - to finish tied for sixth on the leaderboard through 54 holes.

In windy conditions, Spain's Alejandro Del Rey and American duo Johannes Veerman and JJ Spaun had all been tied with Celli and Elvira at 12 under par late in the third round.

Del Rey and Veerman had enjoyed epic days on the course, each shooting low scores of eight-under 64 to shoot up the leaderboard.

Celli, however, rose to make four birdies on his back nine, to jump above the chasing pack, alongside Elvira, and benefitted from an incredible bit of luck on his last hole.

His approach shot ricocheted off a wooden bulkhead lining the stream and somehow missed the water, instead skirting into the greenside bunker. From there he would make birdie to card a third-round 69.

"I'm very happy because today was very tough," the 26-year-old Italian said. "It was windy out there. So I'm happy with how I handled the situation. Sometimes the wind changed a bit, so it wasn't easy.

"I was very patient through the front nine because I knew that on the back nine, I could have like more chances to make some birdies."

Elvira also made a birdie on his last hole, to post a four-under 68, and said after his round he "feels ready" to claim his debut tournament on the DP World Tour.

Plenty of other high-profile players also remain firmly in contention at the top of a bunched leaderboard, with Robert MacIntyre impressing to go five under through what was a flawless, bogey-free back nine, as he rose to tied-11th at 10 under par, alongside Ludvig Åberg, Ryan Fox, Matt Wallace and Sam Bairstow.

"That was a grind out there," Scott, who had to battle to move to finish two shots off the lead, said. "I saw all these good scores up on the board, but it didn't feel like that was really doable.

"It was one step forward and a couple of steps back out there. Very hard to get in a rhythm. Hard to feel like you had a number where you could attack."

Elsewhere, first round co-leader Aaron Rai struggled to advance his score on Saturday, as he finished his day at nine under par. Matt Fitzpatrick, meanwhile, surged up the leaderboard to tie his compatriot, Rai, three back from the lead, alongside halfway leader Ryan Gerard, Alex Noren and Jordan Smith.

McIlroy: I will play aggressively if I need to

It felt like the Northern Irishman was looking for a spark throughout his third round, with McIlroy battling to go one over through his front nine.

The eighth hole has been his nemesis all week, with McIlroy cancelling out an early birdie on the fourth with a bogey on the eighth before adding another on the ninth.

It means McIlroy has gone three over on the eighth hole over his first three rounds.

The reigning Masters champion, who can usurp Patrick Reed at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings with a second-place finish at the top of the leaderboard this week, found his groove, making birdie on the 12th, thanks to some excellent chipping.

He ended his third round with a flourish, striping a three-wood 375 yards down the fairway on the 17th hole on his way to make birdie, before stuffing an approach from 230 yards out to within a few feet of the hole.

McIlroy holed out for eagle to an enormous roar from the fans in the grandstand.

With so many players in contention, and crucial Race to Dubai rankings points in the balance for the world No 2, McIlroy insisted he would play aggressively on the back nine.

"Sunday is going to be interesting," McIlroy said.

"There are a lot of people around the leaders. I think the conditions over the last couple of days are the reason why no one has got away from the pack, just because it has played so tricky and difficult.

"I'll probably try not to look at the leaderboards on the front nine, and if I need to play a little bit more aggressively on the back, I'll do it."

articles.title: ‘Cats go undefeated in non-con play with win over Tulane
articles.summary: MANHATTAN (KSNT) — K-State stays undefeated in non-conference play. The Wildcats defeated the Tulane Green Wave Saturday afternoon, 31-20. Tulane opened up t...
articles.body:
MANHATTAN ( KSNT ) — K-State stays undefeated in non-conference play.

The Wildcats defeated the Tulane Green Wave Saturday afternoon, 31-20.

Tulane opened up the scoring just under the eight-minute mark with a nine-yard quarterback run for a touchdown to lead 7-0.

K-State would not score in the first quarter.

In the second, Luis Rodriguez kicked in a 23-yard field goal to cut the deficit to 7-3.

A few minutes later, running back Jay Harris had a one-yard rush to give the 'Cats the 10-7 lead.

With a little over two minutes remaining, Avery Johnson would pick up a huge 66-yard gain to set up the first down. He'd rush again the following play, this time for seven yards, to grab the touchdown. K-State has the 17-7 lead.

A 58-yard field goal right before the first half would get the Green Wave within a score, as they trailed 17-10.

Harris picked up his second one-yard rushing touchdown to open up the third, building the Wildcat lead to 24-10.

Tulane would grab another big field goal, this time from 53-yards out, to make things 24-13.

In the fourth, Johnson would pick up another rushing touchdown, this one for 12 yards, to extend the 'Cats lead to 31-13.

A 25-yard touchdown reception with just under three minutes left in the game would see Tulane cut the lead down to 31-20, but they would be unable to come any closer as K-State secured the win.

Johnson was 21-for-28 with 227 yards in the air, 152 yards on the ground and two rushing touchdowns.

On the defense, Darien Whitaker picked up 1.5 sacks and 1.5 tackles for loss. Gabe Powers also had 1.5 tackles for loss.

The 'Cats will open up conference play next weekend when they travel out to Cincinnati to take on the Bearcats. Kickoff is set for 6 p.m.

articles.body:
ASHEVILLE, N.C. — Neal Shipley held onto a one-shot lead over Ben Kohles on Saturday in the inaugural Biltmore Championship Asheville, making an eagle and a birdie on the two back-nine par 5s in his third straight bogey-free round.

Shipley had a 21-under 192 total on The Cliffs at Walnut Grove.

"Just going to keep doing what I'm doing," Shipley said. "Keep being me and keep having fun out there. Keep that mindset of going out there, chasing birdies, and trying to get it as low as possible tomorrow."

The PGA Tour rookie also opened with a 65 and had a 62 on Friday in the first of eight tournaments in the FedEx Cup Fall that determine the top 100 in the FedEx Cup who keep full cards for next season.

Shipley entered the week 183rd in the standings. A victory would not only give him a two-year exemption, it would secure him for the more lucrative Championship Series in 2028 when the tour revamps its schedule.

"It would be huge," Shipley said. "It would take a lot of stress off my back, that's for sure. It's one of those things I'm playing really well and I know it's a matter of time for me, so I'm going to give it my best shot tomorrow and lay it all out there and see what happens."

Kohles matched Shipley with a 65, birdieing three of the last four holes. Playing alongside Shipley in the final threesome, Kohles eagled the par-5 third. He's chasing his first PGA Tour title.

"Happy with the day," Kohles said. "Played solid. Took advantage of par 5s, which like I said yesterday, is something you got to do out here on this course."

Shipley hit a 227-yard approach to 7 1/2 to set up the eagle on the par-5 15th. He birdied the par-5 18th and closed with a par.

Eric Cole (64) and Ricky Castillo (65) were tied for third at 17 under. Jacob Bridgeman (64) and Max Greyserman (66) were 16 under.

The tee times were moved up and the players were grouped in threes because of the possibility of late afternoon storms.

The 21-year-old PGA Tour rookie rose up 13 spots on the leaderboard in Asheville thanks to a bogey-free 63 third round.

articles.title: New £1m grant to help protect Gloucestershire green spaces
articles.summary: The cash can be used by local communities to protect threatened green spaces and wildlife sites.
articles.body:
A £1m fund has been set up to help local communities protect threatened green spaces.

The Summerfield Charitable Trust said the money would help groups buy and safeguard local woodlands and wildlife sites when they come up for sale.

It is part of a new initiative from the Gloucestershire Nature and Climate Fund and the Gloucestershire Local Nature Partnership.

"We need an initiative like this now more than ever," said Diane Hill, chair of the Gloucestershire Nature and Climate Fund. "Once an important green space is lost, it can be lost for good."

Hill said: "We know there are people across Gloucestershire who desperately want to protect woodland or wildlife sites in their community but when that land comes up for sale, they simply don't have the time or resources to compete with a private buyer.

"This funding means we can help them when it really matters.

"We can provide money to act quickly, bring in the legal and ecological expertise they need."

Recent examples of communities taking action to protect land include Daisybank , Lott Meadow and Southcourt Green, in Cheltenham, as well as Juniper Hill Field and Heavens Valley in Stroud .

Another was Rodborough Fields, near Stroud, where a public campaign to protect the woodland from development led to it being brought into community ownership.

John Bloxsom, chair of the Rodborough Fields and Frome Banks Preservation Group, said: "It's good news that a fund like this has been set up."

The group successfully bought nine acres of Rodborough Fields thanks to a Crowdfunding campaign that raised £200,000 but now the future of a further 30 acres is uncertain after it was put on the market this summer.

Bloxsom said that their latest bid had been rejected in favour of a rival bid from an unknown party, which was "causing concern in the community".

Angela France, one of the directors at Daisybank CIC, which helped to saved the field in Cheltenham from development last year, said she was "delighted" to hear about the new fund.

"Local green spaces are so important to us now," she said.

"I see more and more local communities getting together to protect them."

She said since buying the land, the group had organised litter picking, butterfly counts and an ecological survey in order to plan how best to maintain the field so that local wildlife could thrive.

A community event is also organised for 24 October to gather views on the future of the field.

The new fund has also been designed to contribute to nature recovery across the county, while addressing unequal access to nature.

David Owen, chair of trustees at The Summerfield Charitable Trust, said the initiative "has the potential to create a lasting legacy for nature, communities and future generations across Gloucestershire".

He added: "Through this investment, we hope to enable communities to act quickly when opportunities arise, protect important natural assets and create benefits for wildlife, health and wellbeing that will endure for many years to come."

articles.title: Online map shows how suitable Guernsey homes are for solar panels
articles.summary: The States of Guernsey says the map will show people how suitable for solar panels their homes are.
articles.body:
An online map has been launched to help islanders understand how suitable their homes are for solar panels.

The States of Guernsey said the map was colour-coded to show the amount of light that solar panels would receive on the island's rooftops across the course of a year.

Roofs with higher potential to generate electricity through solar panels show as dark red, while roof spaces with lower potential are coloured dark blue.

Deputy Adrian Gabriel, said while islanders are encouraged to contact professionals when looking to install solar panels, the map would be a "really helpful tool to get an initial idea on whether the potential for solar is there for householders".

The States said renewable energy provider, Little Green, had spoken to the Committee for the Environment & Infrastructure to highlight the benefits of the tool to people interested in installing solar panels.

Gabriel said the island gets about 30-35% more sunshine than the UK on average. He added: "This free tool makes us well placed to understand how we can better take advantage of the energy we can harness from the sun.

"It's clear that there is a significant opportunity in our island, and this map might just be the catalyst to take Guernsey's solar generation to the next level."

Simon de la Rue, commercial director at Little Green, said: "This map gives an independent, objective check, so any quote can be held to it."

articles.title: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-Offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings discussed the plans for the season-ending Play-Offs, the Strategic Alliance with the PGA Tour and the bright future the tour has within the global game
articles.body:
The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week.

There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.

Matt Fitzpatrick and Bob MacIntyre were among players to express concerns about travelling to the UAE, despite a relaxing of the previous "all but essential travel" guidelines from the UK's Foreign Office, with Kinnings hopeful both events can take place as planned.

"A lot of people are asking and it's an obvious question," Kinnings told Sky Sports . "The reality is we expect every intention to be playing in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

"Work has started and we're building stuff at Yas Links and at the Jumeirah Golf Estates, so our intention is to go ahead.

"We clearly need to keep in touch with travel advisors and other people who help with us, but our plan is definitely to play the Play-Offs in the UAE."

Defending DP World Tour champion Fitzpatrick said on Wednesday that he was "not that comfortable" playing in Dubai, given its proximity to the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, although McIlroy was less concerned.

"If the local governments feel like it's safe to put on these events, they are not going to put their citizens or people visiting in harm's way," McIlroy said after his opening round at the BMW PGA Championship.

"I love the Middle East. I have a lot of friends there and I'm looking forward to going back for sure."

The DP World Tour announced its 2027 schedule at the BMW PGA Championship, with the Flagship Event being held a week later next year and immediately after the centenary Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.

JJ Spaun and Ryan Gerard were among the limited American players to make the trip over to England for the event, despite more spots being available to PGA Tour players, although Kinnings hopes to see more make the journey in the future.

" I think the future schedule will lend itself to that," Kinnings said. "We've got a great working relationship with the PGA Tour and we're working with them on what the future will look like.

"I think the way the schedule's set up, with golf in America stopping at the end of August, we've got the opportunity to shine from September 1 until the end of January. I think that'll mean more of the guys will come and play in great events like this and some of the other tournaments as well."

Kinnings added: "I have to say, I couldn't be more excited. I think it's a huge opportunity for international golf. We clearly have wonderful players and we have an opportunity to shine in the schedule."

The DP World Tour has yet to announce whether it will impose sanctions for its members wishing to play in the new iteration of the LIV Golf League, should LIV 2.0 go ahead as planned in 2027, with Kinnings keen to see the strongest fields possible on his circuit.

"We've been very consistent on the whole question and we're going to continue that way," Kinnings insisted. "What will happen with LIV is entirely speculation, but from our perspective we want to find a balance. As a business, we just love to have the best fields we possibly can with the best players.

"But we're also a member's organisation and our job is purely to make sure we look out for the best interests of the members. We have a wonderful tour, amazing culture and that's because of the players, so nothing's going to change on that front.

"I think we're in a stronger position as we can possibly be. We've got great partners and the future looks bright - we now just need to work out exactly what it looks like."

articles.title: Rory McIlroy stood 230 yards from the 18th green; one 4-iron later the ball stopped inside two feet and changed everything
articles.summary: International Sports News: Rory McIlroy had spent most of Saturday grinding through a frustrating day at Wentworth. Then the back nine happened. A birdie at the 12th. Another at.
articles.body: Rory McIlroy had spent most of Saturday grinding through a frustrating day at Wentworth. Then the back nine happened. A birdie at the 12th. Another at the 17th. And then, standing 230 yards from the 18th green with water lurking between him and glory, he reached for a 4-iron and hit it pure. The ball landed and stopped inside two feet. Tap-in eagle. He signed for a 69, moved to 11 under par, and placed himself two shots behind the leaders heading into Sunday's final round of the 2026 BMW PGA Championship.Why Saturday's eagle felt different from every other shot Rory McIlroy has hit this weekIt was not just the shot. It was the moment it arrived.McIlroy had been on eight under through two rounds, four shots off American Ryan Gerard's lead after a steady but unspectacular start to the week. Friday's 67 was encouraging, not electric. He was in the hunt, but the kind of hunt where you're chasing shadows rather than dictating terms.Saturday changed the tone. He wasn't great early. Wentworth's West Course doesn't offer cheap birdies, and the third round exposed him through stretches where the scorecard wasn't moving. But he stayed patient. That is what McIlroy has learned at this course more than most: the back nine will offer chances, and the last two holes in particular -- both par-5s -- can rewrite your afternoon if you let them.He let them."I think it was a day where you really had to take advantage of the par 5s," McIlroy said. "They were your scoring opportunities."Playing those three back-nine par-5s in four under is how a 69 gets made on a day that looked like it was heading somewhere far less interesting.The shot itself: What a committed 4-Iron over water actually looks likeThere is a version of that 18th hole that has swallowed rounds whole. Water short of the green, a green that rewards precision over power, the kind of approach that invites a cautious lay-up when your card isn't working and a brave line when it is. McIlroy chose the brave line."It was a perfect 4-iron where I could just hold it into the wind slightly," he said. "I just needed to stand up and make a good, committed swing, and I did."The word 'committed' is doing a lot of work there. From 230 yards, into the wind, over water, in the third round of one of European golf's biggest events — the difference between a committed swing and a hesitant one can be the difference between two feet and a lake. McIlroy made the swing, and the ball behaved accordingly."Obviously a great way to finish the day and keep myself within touching distance of the leaders," he added.Two shots. That's all that separates him from Filippo Celli and Manuel Elvira, who share the lead at 13 under par. JJ Spaun, the 2025 US Open champion, sits in a group at 12 under. McIlroy is tied at 11 under with a group that includes LIV star Joaquin Niemann and former world number one Adam Scott. The leaderboard entering Sunday is as compressed as it gets.The race to Dubai Subplot that makes Sunday even biggerYou can't properly understand what McIlroy is chasing at Wentworth without understanding what happened on Friday to Patrick Reed.Reed arrived at Wentworth leading the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai standings by just under 1,000 points over McIlroy. The American -- who quit LIV Golf at the start of 2026 and returned to the European circuit, winning the Dubai Desert Classic and the Qatar Masters along the way -- had been building a compelling case for becoming only the second American after Collin Morikawa to top the rankings.Friday ended that, at least for this week. Reed opened his second round by carding a triple bogey on the first hole, then doubled the fourth and eighth. He was nine over through nine holes. Then, attempting a recovery shot from the rough on the ninth, his club made contact with what appeared to be a tree root and came flying out of his hands. He walked off the 10th tee after hitting his drive and didn't come back. Wrist injury. Withdrawal.It was a brutal end to his week, and it opened a door for McIlroy."Unfortunately he's pulled out this week, which gives me an opportunity to try to claw back some ground," McIlroy said, though he was careful to add: "I'm motivated regardless of who it is."The mathematics are clear. The BMW PGA Championship is worth 9,000 Race to Dubai points. A solo second or better here would be enough for McIlroy to leap over Reed and take the top spot. A win would be decisive. And McIlroy isn't thinking about points alone."I have a big opportunity tomorrow on both fronts," he said.A tournament McIlroy has won before, a course he has loved since he was 10Twelve years. That is how long it has been since McIlroy won at Wentworth. He took the BMW PGA Championship in 2014, and the course has stayed close to him ever since -- in a deeply personal way, not just as a venue on a schedule.He lives on the Wentworth estate when he is in the UK. He first came here as a ten-year-old, watching the old World Match Play Championship during school half-term with his parents. The place has layers of memory for him that most courses simply do not."I came here for the first time as a 10-year-old to watch the World Match Play all the way back in the day. It was always half-term," McIlroy said. "I always came with my mum and dad and watched this one. Fast forward, I've won this event, I've played a lot here and we now have a house on the estate as well. This place has a lot of history for me."That history matters because it speaks to motivation beyond rankings and points. He genuinely wants this one. And he's also chasing something bigger on the DP World Tour. A win here, combined with Reed's absence, would put him in position to claim a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title -- matching Colin Montgomerie's mark."I'd love to win this tournament again. It's been a long time, 12 years. Hopefully I have a good chance and give myself a real chance at it again."Why Sunday at Wentworth could be specialThe group around McIlroy makes Sunday worth watching beyond just his story. Adam Scott, 46, is chasing something too. He has never won at Wentworth and has spoken openly about how badly he wants to change that."Oh, it would be so special," Scott said. "I rate this tournament so highly. I've enjoyed playing here for a lot of years now, and with strong connections to European golf, I would love to etch my name into the history here at Wentworth."Celli and Elvira are in front and will not be thinking about giving ground. Spaun, the reigning US Open champion, knows how to close. The leaderboard entering Sunday at the DP World Tour's flagship event is genuinely wide open.And McIlroy arrives two back having just hit what he called a perfect shot at the hardest moment of his day. Patience rewarded, he said. That is how he wants to play Sunday."I stayed as patient as I could and feel like that patience was rewarded over the last few holes," McIlroy said. "Good birdie on 12. I always feel like the end of this golf course gives you a chance to salvage maybe a tougher, frustrating day, and I was able to do that."Two shots. That is what Sunday starts with. It started with a 4-iron from 230 yards and a ball that stopped inside two feet, and now the whole thing comes down to eighteen more holes on a course where McIlroy grew up watching his heroes and then became one himself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Manuel Elvira acaricia la victoria en el BMW PGA Championship
articles.standfirst: El cántabro llegó a liderar en solitario el emblemático torneo británico del DP World Tour pero acabó a dos golpes del estadounidense JJ Spaun
articles.summary: El cántabro llegó a liderar en solitario el emblemático torneo británico del DP World Tour pero acabó a dos golpes del estadounidense JJ Spaun
articles.body: Manuel Elvira ha firmado el mejor torneo de su carrera profesional pero no pudo coronarlo con un sonado triunfo en el BMW PGA Championship. El golfista cántabro acabó finalmente segundo con 273 golpes (-15), a dos del estadounidense JJ Spaun, ganador del US Open 2025. A sus 30 años, el menor de los Elvira llegaba colíder a esta cuarta y última ronda y llegó a mandar en solitario cuando apenas quedaban cinco hoyos pero un postrero doble bogey en el 18 -tras un gran eagle en el 17-, un par 5 que jugó sin duda tensionado por la dimensión del posible triunfo, le condenó ante un Spaun que acabó con cuatro birdies en los cinco últimos hoyos. Este es el mejor resultado de Manuel Elvira en un torneo del DP World Tour, en el que nunca había acabado en el podio virtual, con el cuarto puesto del Magical Kenya Open de 2024 como mejor resultado hasta hoy. Sí había sido tercero en el ISCO Championship de 2025, cita del PGA Tour. Manuel Elvira acabó empatado en la segunda plaza con el norirlandés Rory McIlroy, ganador en el Wentworth Club en 2014; el inglés Aaron Rai, vencedor este año del PGA Championship, y el australiano Adam Scott, de 46 años y ganador del Masters en 2013. Alejandro del Rey fue decimoquinto con 276 golpes (-12) tras una última vuelta muy irregular con cinco birdies, tres bogeys y un doble bogey, con Eugenio López-Chacarra firmando otra buena actuación en el puesto 21 y 277 golpes. Miguel Ángel Jiménez, en 2008, sigue siendo por tanto el último español en levantar este trofeo en un torneo en el que Jon Rahm ha acabado dos veces segundo antes de firmar un pésimo resultado este año. Manuel Elvira no pudo emular a su hermano mayor Nacho, vencedor de tres torneos del DP World Tour, para convertirse en la sexta pareja de hermanos, y la tercera española tras Antonio y Germán Garrido y Seve y Manuel Ballesteros, en ser ganadores de torneos en el circuito europeo.

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship 2026: JJ Spaun snatches victory at Wentworth, as Rory McIlroy comes unstuck despite late surge
articles.summary: JJ Spaun claimed a two-shot victory in the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth after Manuel Elvira made a double-bogey the 18th hole to cede victory to the American; Rory McIlroy finished tied-second; watch the Open de France live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday
articles.body:
An utterly thrilling final round of golf unfolded, with multiple players, including Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Elvira, racing to the finish line, but all struggled to pull away from the pack.

There was heartbreak for Elvira, who had the chance to leapfrog Spaun at the top of the leaderboard after tying the 2025 US Open champion with an eagle on the 17th hole.

With Spaun already in the clubhouse at 17 under, the Spaniard, who is ranked 294th in the Official World Golf Rankings, needed a birdie on the 18th to win his first DP World Tour title, but he stumbled, finding a fairway bunker with his tee shot before sending his bunker shot well past the green.

He attempted to chip back on but agonisingly sent his shot into another bunker before ultimately confirming Spaun's two-stroke win with a double-bogey.

Elvira would tie McIlroy, Rai and Adam Scott at 15 under par for second place, as 13 players would finish within three shots of the lead.

McIlroy mixed in moments of brilliance with a few critical errors. The Northern Irishman also struggled to make birdie putts, but surged in his back nine, making birdies on holes 12, 14 and 17, to post a final-round score of 68.

Rai, who had taken the joint-lead after the first round, was impressive throughout his week at Wentworth, and the Englishman once again put the gas on as he tried to pull away from the chasing pack of players, taking the clubhouse lead before Spaun with a final-round 66.

Open champion Ryan Fox would join Matt Fitzpatrick, Joost Luiten and Filippo Celli tied for sixth place at 14 under.

Spaun, who was omitted from Brandt Snedeker's Team USA Presidents Cup squad, felt he had "taken care of business this week", showing his patience to bounce back from an early bogey on the first to card six birdies, and end with a score of 67.

"We [him and captain Brandt Snedeker] haven't spoken," the 36-year-old said. "But yeah, I played with a huge chip on my shoulder.

"I'm so delighted to be here and just play this event. I've always wanted to do this. The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you kind of have, determination.

"Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple of weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserved to be on that team.

"I took care of my business this week, so all the best to my mates next week at Medinah, but I'll be on the couch watching."

Elvira 'devastated, but buoyed by performance

Elvira crouched down in frustration after missing his first putt on the 18th, cutting a shattered figure before eventually holing out for a double-bogey.

Despite coming up short, the Spaniard explained he was chuffed with his performance.

"Devastating that I hit the wrong shot at the right time on the lay-up and left myself the toughest shot in the fairway bunker, and I wasn't able to pull it off," he said.

"I've played some of the best golf, probably, of my life. I was in contention and I wasn't really that nervous. It's been a great week and I'm really glad for it."

McIlroy: I wish I had some of those putts back

After struggling to make an impact on the front nine, McIlroy found trouble on the 12th before producing an epic recovery shot around a cluster of trees, eventually going on to make birdie.

It was the spark the Northern Irishman needed, as he followed it with further birdies on the 14th and 17th. He came undone on the 18th, however, finding a fairway bunker before missing a putt for birdie.

"I wish I had some of those putts back," McIlroy said on his putting woes.

"But I have to be encouraged with where my game is at.

"Hit the ball really well. Hit the best I hit it during the course of the week and am encouraged with the signs that my game is going and just have to keep working at it."

The next DP World Tour event is the FedEx Open de France, which gets under way on Thursday at Le Golf National, the venue for Europe's 2018 Ryder Cup triumph.

Meanwhile, Team USA will chase a record-extending 11th consecutive victory over the International Team at the Presidents Cup, which also begins on Thursday at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

articles.title: La Sella Open 2026: Charlotte Heath bounces back after blowing four-shot lead to claim first LET title
articles.summary: Charlotte Heath clinched her debut Ladies European Tour title at the La Sella Open, bouncing back after letting a four-shot lead disappear to finish two shots clear of the field; watch LET golf live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The 24-year-old rookie started the final round with a four-shot advantage and, despite seeing her lead disappear during a tense Sunday afternoon, she held her composure to card a final-round 73 and finish at 10 under par, two shots clear of the field.

After three weather-affected days, gusting winds continued to add an extra layer of difficulty, and set the stage for a thrilling finale at one of the LET's premier events.

Heath's front nine featured a solitary bogey at the fifth as she turned in 37, while Germany's Helen Briem mounted a strong challenge and briefly drew level at nine under par through 13 holes. However, Briem immediately dropped a shot at the next, allowing Heath to reclaim the outright lead.

As Briem and Shannon Tan of Singapore slipped back on the closing stretch, Italy's Alessandra Fanali posted the clubhouse target at eight under par.

The strongest challenge ultimately came from Englishwoman Alice Hewson, who surged into contention with a birdie finish. Standing over an eagle putt on the 18th that would have tied the lead, Hewson narrowly missed before tapping in for birdie, joining Fanali at eight under par.

Heath was left needing a composed finish to seal the biggest victory of her career.

On the final hole, Heath split the fairway with her drive before finding a difficult position to the right of the green with her second shot. Unfazed, she pitched to nine feet and confidently rolled in a birdie putt to cap a remarkable week, ending her week with two birdies and two bogeys across the back nine.

The victory earns Heath her first LET title, a £128,722 (€150,000) winner's cheque and an unforgettable breakthrough moment in her rookie season.

"It's incredible," said Heath. "This year, I've gone out in the leading group twice before, so I guess it's third-time lucky.

"It was incredible having Alex [Long] on the bag. He kept me so calm and just reminded me that I'd played good golf all week. When the pressure is on, negative thoughts can creep in, so I'm very, very happy to get it done."

Heath admitted the mental challenge was as demanding as any shot she faced.

"You probably didn't want to be in my head on that golf course today," she said. "I was thinking I was going to shank it, hook it, pull it. You never know. Alex kept the ship steady all day."

Hewson, meanwhile, reflected on another strong performance at a venue she has long enjoyed.

"It's been a really solid week," she said. "I played some nice golf out there and probably didn't hole as many putts as I would have liked.

"La Sella is always one of my favourite stops on tour and having my whole family here made it even more special."

The LET travels to Italy for the Buccellati Ladies Italian Open at Golf Club Milano, which will be played from September 25-27.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy switches focus to battle with Patrick Reed for Race to Dubai title after near-miss at BMW PGA Championship
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy moved within 307.76 points of Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai rankings with a tied-second finish at the BMW PGA Championship; McIlroy is looking to win the Order of Merit for an eighth time; JJ Spaun claimed a two-shot win at Wentworth
articles.body:
McIlroy went into the final round two strokes back at Wentworth, where he recovered from failing to convert numerous birdie chances to briefly grab a share of the lead during a thrilling final round.

The world No 2 stumbled to a closing par to post a final-round 68 and finish in tied-second on 15 under, two strokes behind winner JJ Spaun, leaving McIlroy with a fourth runner-up finish at the DP World Tour's flagship event since his 2014 win.

"I had my chances out there!" McIlroy told Sky Sports . "I felt like I hit the ball really well - probably the best I've hit it all week.

"Had good chances on two, three, five, eight, nine, 10, 13, the last. I felt like I hit good putts but, a bit like last week [Amgen Irish Open], I was just not seeing the lines that well.

"I struggled with some of the reads today and I hit some good putts that didn't go in. I holed a couple coming down the stretch but I think the story of the week was that I didn't hole as much as I should have.

"If I did, it would have been a different story."

Will Reed stop McIlroy's Race to Dubai title bid?

McIlroy ending in a four-way share of second earned him 532 Race to Dubai points and moved him within 308 of Reed, who withdrew mid-round on Friday due to injury, in the season-long standings.

Reed had said he was looking forward to a battle with McIlroy, who will next feature at the DP World India Championship from October 15-18 before the two season-ending DP World Tour Play-Offs in the Middle East.

The Northern Irishman has topped the Order of Merit in four consecutive seasons and is looking to finish No 1 again, which would pull McIlroy level with Colin Montgomerie's all-time tally of eight Race to Dubai titles.

"As soon as The Open was over, really that was the goal for the rest of the year," McIlroy added. "I would obviously love to do it [win the Race to Dubai].

"For Patrick, it was unfortunate this week. Hopefully he's okay and he can play what he needs to going in to really make it a good battle, but I'm excited.

"I'll keep working on my game over the next three weeks, then hopefully have a strong end to the season and give myself a great chance at that eighth one."

McIlroy's runner-up finish at Wentworth follows previous seconds there in 2018, 2022 and 2024, leaving him still searching for his first worldwide win since successfully defending his Masters title in April.

"I think McIlroy left a little bit behind him on the greens - he had loads of chances," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports .

"It was surprising for a guy who has really improved his putting over the past couple of years and looks so good over them, but he seemed to miss putt after putt after putt.

"I don't think he has played his best golf from tee to green, I'd rate him 3.5 out of five for what he's capable of. It's almost like he couldn't get out of the starting blocks but still finishes tied-second - it's incredible and shows just how much talent he has."

McIlroy is next scheduled to feature at the DP World India Championship from October 15-18, before further appearances at the Abu Dhabi Championship (November 5-8) and the DP World Tour Championship (November 12-15).

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship: How JJ Spaun used Team USA snub for Presidents Cup as motivation for dramatic Wentworth victory
articles.summary: JJ Spaun claimed a two-shot win at the BMW PGA Championship; Spaun discussed missing out on Team USA's Presidents Cup side and why him and his wife are obsessed with Jeremy Clarkson after his debut victory at Wentworth
articles.body:
Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports , with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.

"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.

"We [him and Snedeker] haven't spoken. I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week, but everything happens for a reason. I'm so delighted to be here and just to even play this event.

"The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you have. Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team.

"I took care of my business this week, so all the best to the team next week at Medinah - I'll be watching from my couch!"

Spaun said he had good conversations with Snedeker during the qualification campaign and believed he would feature at Medinah, but was handed the unwanted news in a short phone call after the season-ending Tour Championship.

"It was like a 45-second phone call," Spaun revealed in his press conference. "Just said I wasn't on the team and said I was the odd man out. I wished him luck and that was it.

"It [past conversations] led me to believe that I would make the team."

Spaun added: "I was pretty determined this week to kind of prove something. My whole career, I've kind of had to do that. I wasn't given scholarships. I had to earn my PGA Tour card the hard way. I was never given sponsor invite opportunities - I just had to do everything the hard way.

"Being left off was obviously for a reason. I don't know what that reason was, but I'm here now and there was a reason why we're here. My caddie kept telling me that and it's crazy how this has happened."

Why did Spaun celebrate win with a Jeremy Clarkson mask?

Spaun celebrated victory with his wife, Melody, who brought a mask of broadcaster Jeremy Clarkson around the course during various points of the week.

"We've grown fond of him [Jeremy Clarkson], along with the English culture," Spaun explained. "We actually take holidays in December in the Cotswolds and we really enjoy his show [Clarkson's Farm]. I went to his pub The Farmer's Dog, with the hopes to catch a glimpse of him, but he wasn't around.

"Yeah, she [his wife Melody] said we would have a surprise guest following this week if I competed in the tournament and sure enough it was Thursday morning - I see the face of Jeremy Clarkson and her holding it.

"Jeremy was there in spirit and I think he brought me good fortune!"

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship: Manuel Elvira devastated as JJ Spaun triumphs at Wentworth
articles.summary: Manuel Elvira choked back the tears as an elated JJ Spaun celebrated becoming only the third US player to win the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
articles.body:
17 JJ Spaun (US); -15 M Elvira (Spa), R McIlroy (NI), A Scott (Aus), A Rai (Eng)

Selected others : -14 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), R Fox (NZ); -13 R MacIntyre (Sco), M Wallace (Eng), A Sullivan (Eng); -12 A Noren (Swe), R Fisher (Eng); -11 S Lowry (Ire) A Fitzpatrick (Eng); -10 V Hovland (Nor), L Aberg (Swe), J Niemann (Chi), T Hatton (Eng)

Golf can be a cruel game. As Spain's Manuel Elvira choked back the tears on Sunday, just a short distance away an elated JJ Spaun celebrated becoming only the third player from the United States to win the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

The 2025 US Open champion joins Billy Horschel and the legendary Arnold Palmer on a storied list of winners that also includes Tony Jacklin, Sir Nick Faldo, Seve Ballesteros, Jose Maria Olazabal and Rory McIlroy.

However, it was hard not to feel sympathy for Elvira, the unknown 30-year-old from Santander.

Ranked 294th in the world, this had looked like being the moment he had longed for when he stepped on to the final tee with a first victory in his sights - straight off the back of outrageous eagle on the 17th.

Having twice made birdies on the friendly par five this week, a third was hardly implausible - while a par would have ensured a play-off with Spaun, already in the clubhouse at 17 under par.

Instead Elvira, who opted for an iron off the tee, found a fairway bunker when he took the conservative option to lay up.

To compound matters he then missed the green with his approach, almost finding the grandstand, and duffed his fourth into the sand after being given a free drop.

Once he escaped he took a further two putts, and his double-bogey seven finish deprived him of even ending the tournament in outright second place.

"[It was] devastating that I hit the wrong shot at the right time on the lay up and left myself the toughest shot in the fairway bunker, and wasn't able to pull it off," Elvira said.

"I've played some of the best golf probably of my life."

While it was not at the level of Jean Van de Velde's implosion at the 1999 Open Championship or, more recently, Jordan Spieth's misadventures in the 2016 Masters - it nevertheless made for difficult viewing.

And his brother Ignacio - who had earlier finished in a tie for 44th - was left to console his younger sibling as they walked off the 18th green.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, former Europe Solheim Cup player Trish Johnson said: "It's a truly awful feeling. No more than 20 minutes ago he's got this huge dream.

"To watch that unfold on 18 was really, in golfing terms, quite tragic. What he has to remember is how he put himself in that position.

"In a big event like this the chances are we'll never see him in that position to win this calibre of tournament ever again, and that's very sad."

As Elvira trudged away after ending on 15 under alongside major champions McIlroy, Adam Scott and Aaron Rai, which in any other circumstances could have been considered a triumph, Spaun was already rejoicing his first title outside of the US.

While that will earn him a hefty pay cheque of about £1.1m, he said his omission from the US Presidents Cup - a tournament where America face a rest-of-the-world team, excluding Europe - had been the driving force behind his success.

Spaun outlined that he had been given the news in a 45-second phone call, in which he was told he was the "odd man out".

"I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week but everything happens for a reason," said Spaun, who carded a five-under 67 on Sunday, crucially including four birdies in the concluding five holes.

"My whole career, I've kind of had to do that. I wasn't given scholarships. I had a walk-on. I had to earn my PGA Tour card the hard way. I was never given sponsor invite opportunities. I just had to do everything the hard way.

"Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing, and you know, I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team."

Spirit of Clarkson & McIlroy's Race to Dubai consolation

One amusing aspect of Spaun's round was seeing his wife Melody walking around the grounds of the famous Surrey club with a Jeremy Clarkson mask.

"We've grown fond of him - along with the English culture, we actually take holidays in December in the Cotswolds - and we really enjoy his show [Clarkson's Farm]," Spaun added.

"I went to his pub, with the hopes of catching a glimpse of him, but he wasn't around.

"My wife said we would have a surprise guest following me this week if I competed in the tournament and, sure enough, I see the face of Jeremy Clarkson and her holding it. Jeremy was there in spirit and I think he brought me good fortune."

While Spaun's putter ran hot, McIlroy made five birdies and a bogey on Sunday, in a round that also included four birdie misses from inside 10 feet.

The one consolation for the six-time major winner is that he made a huge dent in Patrick Reed's lead in the Race to Dubai standings as he goes for a record-equalling eighth title.

"I'm excited. I have three events until the end of my DP World Tour season. I'm not sure what Patrick's schedule looks like coming up, but I feel like I have enough opportunities," McIlroy said.

"I'm excited for the opportunity, and it would be obviously amazing to match Monty's record."

articles.title: PGA Tour: Jacob Bridgeman races to Biltmore Championship victory to provide Team USA form boost for Presidents Cup
articles.summary: Jacob Bridgeman won the Genesis Invitational in February and is now a multiple PGA Tour winner; Bridgeman will represent Team USA for the first time at the Presidents Cup, live on Thursday from 5pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Bridgeman, named among Brandt Snedeker's captain's picks for Team USA to face the International Team at Medinah, overturned a five-shot deficit during a low-scoring final day in Asheville, North Carolina.

The world No 29 raced through the field by carding an eagle and eight birdies during a bogey-free 61 at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove, lifting him to 26 under and two shots clear of compatriot Ben James, who matched his 61.

Bridgeman, 26, birdied three of his opening four holes and holed from 10 feet to eagle the par-five eighth, before picking up a shot at the 10th and posting three more in a row from the 13th.

He needed to play his last three holes in three under to card his first sub-60 round on the PGA Tour, but a birdie at the par-five 17th and closing par was enough for a second PGA Tour win of the year.

"It's a dream come true," Bridgeman said about representing Team USA, live from Thursday on Sky Sports . "There is so much individualness in this sport, but to be able to play as a team and the United States is just amazing.

"Everybody is pumped. It's getting really real. We're all getting super excited!"

Overnight leader Neal Shipley finished three strokes back in tied-third alongside Ricky Castillo, with fellow American JT Poston narrowly missing out on a '59 round' as he jumped into a share of fifth alongside Jackson Koivun, who will also feature in the Presidents Cup.

"At the end of the day it was a great round of golf, a new career low out here," Poston said, having two-putted from 25 feet to par his final hole as he carded a 60. "As much as I would like to shoot that magical 59 number, which I've never done, there are so many positives to take away."

Ireland's Seamus Power ended six strokes back in a share of seventh, with England's Marco Penge - a notable absentee from the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - finishing in a share of 10th after a final-round 67.

articles.title: Just when Jacob Bridgeman didn’t think his year could get better, he wins near home in front of family
articles.summary: Jacob Bridgeman had already accomplished his three goals this year. A victory at the Biltmore Championship in front of family and friends was icing on the ca...
articles.body:
By lunchtime on Sunday, U.S. Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker may have had a pit in his stomach. If that was the case, by the time dinner came around, that indigestion had likely subsided.

J.J. Spaun talked all week from England about how he felt snubbed, that at No. 17 in the world and having won a PGA Tour event this year, he believed he had done enough to warrant wearing red, white and blue for Snedeker this week at Medinah.

With a chip on his shoulder, Spaun topped a stacked field at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth—one that included Rory McIlroy, who tied for second place—and said Snedeker called him the "odd man out" a couple weeks ago during their phone call.

Hours later in Asheville, N.C., two men who Snedeker picked instead of Spaun—Jacob Bridgeman and Jackson Koivun—were making birdies aplenty. Bridgeman made eight birdies and an eagle to shoot 10-under 61 and win the Biltmore Championship, his second tour victory this year after collecting the Genesis Invitational at Riviera. Koivun, the new pro who won the 3M Open in Minnesota, rallied to shoot 65 and tied for fifth place.

"Just wanted to get in kind of a competitive feel again," said the 26-year-old Bridgeman, who, at No. 29 in the world ranking was the best player in the field. "I had a couple weeks off. Played a bunch of golf in there, practiced a ton, so just kind of wanted to get the competitive reps in and see where my game was, and I'm pretty pleased."

He's not the only one. There was a whole team at Medinah in Chicago waiting for him and Koivun to join them. So Bridgeman quickly wrapped up duties and interviews as the tournament champion and the two jumped on a plane to head north.

It's been a whirlwind year for Bridgeman. He started the year ranked 81st in the world and still, believing in himself, he made three lofty goals: to win a tournament, qualify for the Tour Championship at East Lake and play in the Presidents Cup.

The victory this week was gravy. He lives 65 miles south in Greenville, S.C., attended Clemson and had his parents, wife, cousins and friends were all tracking his every move Sunday at the Biltmore. They all were rewarded by watching the best putter on tour put together another stellar performance on the greens, gaining more than 8 shots with the flatstick against the field for the week.

Opening rounds of 66-67 at the Cliffs at Walnut Grove had him barely keep pace before a third-round 64 moved him within a few shots of the top. On Sunday, Bridgeman birdied three of the first four holes, rolled in a 10-footer for eagle on the eighth hole and was squarely in the hunt.

But there were still a lot of contenders, as Bridgeman was tied with J.T. Poston, Ben James, Ricky Castillo and Neal Shipley with nine holes remaining. Poston was farther along in his round and had a putt for 59 on the last but settled for 60. Shipley and Castillo simply didn't make enough birdies to keep pace, but James birdies Nos. 15-17 to shoot a 61 of his own, although it was two shots short in a solo second-place finish.

"I wasn't really thinking about winning," said James, 23, the recent Virginia grad who earned tour status via the PGA Tour University rankings. "I knew that it would probably take something in the 50s.

"Still played a heck of a round of golf and looking forward to keeping the momentum going to Utah."

Bridgeman unloaded with three consecutive birdies on 13, 14 and 15 and had grabbed control. With another at 17 the only thing in question was the margin of victory. It was two as he ended with a 26-under-par 258 total.

"It was my goal today to get off to a hot start and see where I was at, and I just kept it rolling," he said. "I felt like when I turned I just made enough ground. Then it was kind of a tournament between all of us. Didn't feel like I had to chase anymore.

"Then, yeah, the putter was just rolling well all week. Seeing the lines great. Made a ton of birdies and some crucial par saves. Really pleased with my game."

Captain Snedeker would approve this message.

articles.title: 3 overreactions to the Vikings' Week 2 victory over the Bears
articles.summary: It was ugly, but the Vikings went into Chicago and beat the Bears.
articles.body:
It was an ugly performance, but the Minnesota Vikings stormed into Soldier Field and defeated the Chicago Bears 9-3. A downpour from the skies made conditions difficult, but this defense was able to slow down Chicago's elite offense. Here are three overreactions from Minnesota's week two victory.

Dallas Turner has ascended into superstardom

Dallas Turner was excellent in week one against the Green Bay Packers , and followed it up with an even better performance today. Turner ended the day with nine QB pressures, five total tackles, and two sacks. This year, Turner has five sacks, which will end the week toward the top of the NFL. Turner came into the year under immense pressure, and he has lived up to the billing.

Speaking of living up to the billing, this was the coming-out party for defensive tackle Caleb Banks. Banks had a great showing today, finishing with six total tackles, including a tackle for loss. There is still a need for consistency in his game, but we saw significantly more flashes than we saw last week.

We obviously can't wait for Jordan Mason to return from IR, but Aaron Jones showed today he is more than capable of holding down the ground game. Jones had 23 carries for 105 yards, which is such a breath of fresh air compared to years past. He did appear to get banged up in the second half, so we will wait to see the severity of his injury.

articles.title: Trey'Dez Green injury update: LSU tight end avoids surgery per mother's post
articles.summary: Here's the latest injury updates on LSU starting tight end Trey'Dez Green, who sustained an apparent leg injury in Saturday's loss to Ole Miss.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin and LSU appear to have dodged a serious long-term injury with starting tight end Trey'Dez Green .

That, however, doesn't mean the Tigers will be without Green for some time.

In a post on social media from his mother, Green will not require surgery for the apparent leg injury that he sustained in the fourth quarter of Saturday's loss to Mississippi , as the MRI he received on Sunday "showed nothing is torn," but that he'll "miss some games" due to the injury.

"MRI showed nothing is torn, tho he has some bad sprains and bruises. No surgery needed. God said time, treatment & rest. Yes he will miss games, and that's okay. Most importantly is getting better, everything else will fall in place," Green's mother wrote on the post on Facebook .

Green went down with a lower-body injury in the fourth quarter after taking a pair of low hits from Ole Miss defenders. The injury came at the end of a 19-yard catch he caught a pass across the middle of the field from Sam Leavitt during LSU 's eventual drive that tied the game at 24-24 on a field goal.

LSU, which dropped to No. 11 in the latest US LBM Coaches Poll , would go on to lose to Ole Miss 32-24 after Leavitt's final pass of the night was deflected and then intercepted in the end zone. The Tigers host No. 20 Texas A&M at 6:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Sept. 26 at Tiger Stadium.

Green appeared to have sustained a leg injury in the second half of Saturday's game against Ole Miss. He took several hits at the end of a catch and was down on the field for several moments getting tended to by officials.

He walked off toward LSU's sidelines with the help of two members of the Tigers' medical staff and was seen on ABC's cameras in serious pain. He had a limp in his walk as well. He did not return to the game and was later seen on the sidelines using crutches while in street clothes.

Here's a look at the play that Green got injured on:

What did Lane Kiffin say about Trey'Dez Green's injury?

Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Kiffin said that Dashawn Spears and Green's injuries were "more impactful than the loss" that the Tigers took on Saturday night in Oxford.

"The injuries are more impactful than the loss to (Ole Miss)," Kiffin said. "In two of the more dynamic, irreplaceable players in Dashawn Spears and Trey'Dez Green walking around on crutches. That doesn't feel good."

Despite missing the end of the game, Green still finished as LSU's leading receiver with four receptions for 60 yards. His longest reception of the night came in the third quarter on a third-and-11 when he picked up 23 yards on a pass to the left sideline from Sam Leavitt.

articles.title: 3 big things from Packers' win over Jets: LVN erupts, Skky Moore shines
articles.summary: Three big things from the Packers' win over the Jets: Lukas Van Ness, Skky Moore and more OL injuries.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers scored 10 points in the fourth quarter to erase a 17-7 deficit and won in overtime on Trey Smack's 26-yard field goal, beating the New York Jets by a 20-17 final and snapping the team's six-game losing streak dating back to last season. Instead of heading home at 0-2, the Packers will go into Week 3 with an even 1-1 record and a chance to build on Sunday's palate-cleansing, comeback victory at MetLife Stadium.

The win wasn't pretty, but an ugly win beats a pretty loss, especially when a team hasn't tasted a victory since December of last year. The first 50 minutes weren't good enough, but Matt LaFleur's team finished when it mattered.

The big things from the Packers' win over the Jets:

The Packers had to win this football game and avoid an 0-2 start, but the far-reaching implications of the injuries along the offensive line could define the rest of the season. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, by far the line's best player, went down with what could be a season-ending knee injury. Later, Aaron Banks , the line's most experienced player, departed with a new toe injury. How does an already questionable offensive line survive these never-ending injuries? A big opportunity now exists for 2025 second-round pick Anthony Belton and 2026 fifth-round pick Jager Burton. But there is no way to spin this one positively. The Packers offensive line is in big trouble, and it's likely the line will be inconsistent at best and a major, unavoidable weakness at worst over the rest of the season. A football team can overcome a lot and be successful over a 17-game season, but an offensive line that is teetering on disaster every week will be a tough hurdle to clear for the Packers.

Week 1 provided signs of the coming eruption from edge rusher Lukas Van Ness , but no one could have predicted such a thoroughly dominant performance from the 13th overall pick in the 2023 draft. LVN produced a career-high nine pressures, per Next Gen Stats, and he was in on two sacks of Geno Smith and a 4th-and-1 stop. At times he was un-blockable, especially during big moments in the contest. LVN also finished with 10 total tackles, including a few run stops and a crunching tackle on special teams. Micah Parsons will eventually return, likely next month, and the Packers could have a pair of difference-making edge rushers the rest of the way. Jonathan Gannon's defense has held offenses to 4.0 yards or fewer per play during each of the first two weeks. Making LVN's performance all the sweeter: He was selected with the Jets' first-round pick in 2013, which was swapped with the Packers in the Aaron Rodgers trade.

Trey Smack got the walk-off, game-winning field goal, but the special teams star on Sunday at MetLife Stadium was returner Skyy Moore, who ripped off a 43-yard kickoff return in the first half and then provided a game-changing play in the fourth quarter with a 63-yard punt return that set up the game-tying field goal. Moore is consistent return to return, and his ability to flip the field with an explosive return is exactly what the Packers needed on special teams. His acquisition on a one-year deal as a free agent has completely revamped the Packers return game. Given the struggles of the offense on Sunday, it's hard to imagine the Packers winning the game without Moore. Keep this in mind: the Packers didn't have a single kick return over 36 yards or a single punt return over 20 yards last season.

articles.title: Jets news: Aaron Glenn admits crucial decisions went completely over his head
articles.summary: The New York Jets took home a win in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. In Week 2, they had a chance to upset Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Unfortunate...
articles.body:
The New York Jets took home a win in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. In Week 2, they had a chance to upset Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers . Unfortunately, head coach Aaron Glenn watched as his team lost to the Packers in overtime.

Glenn came under fire after the game for his clock management. There were two specific moments that drew the ire of fans. One came at the end of regulation, when timeouts were not used. Then, in overtime, Glenn and the Jets elected to take the ball first.

"I did not consider using (the timeout) at that point at all. I want to go back and really look at it, to be honest with you. They took the penalty on that… At that point, I didn't want to put ourself in the position where we take the time out. Just let it end," Glenn said of the end of regulation situation , via SNY Jets.

"Usually, if you can get yourself in a situation like that, you can control the clock. You can control how they play offense once you go and score… We just didn't do a good job in that situation," the Jets head coach said of his overtime decision .

The Jets had a lead in this contest. In fact, they held a 17-7 lead over the Packers in the fourth quarter. However, Green Bay stormed all the way back to force the extra quarter. They went on to win thanks to a Trey Smack 26-yard field goal.

The Jets certainly wanted to win this one and head into Week 3 undefeated. Instead, Glenn will face his former team, the Detroit Lions , on the road on September 27, looking to avoid falling below .500.

articles.title: Packers’ Matt LaFleur Under Fire Despite Snapping Losing Streak
articles.summary: CBS Sports' Garrett Podell argued Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur should be feeling the heat after an ugly 1-1 start to the regular season. The pos...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers escaped New Jersey with a 20-17 overtime victory against the New York Jets on Sunday.

The cliché "a win is a win" seemed to be the right label for the Week 2 victory. Really all that matters is the Packers ended a six-game losing streak.

But Packers head coach Matt LaFleur still received plenty of criticism from CBS Sports' Garrett Podell, who argued Green Bay 's sloppy start should have the head coach feeling the heat.

"Green Bay became the first team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to win a game with under 200 total yards (199), 10-plus penalties (14 for 133 yards) and no takeaways, per CBS Sports Research," wrote Podell. "Teams in this exact situation prior to the Packers' Week 2 overtime win on Sunday were 0-38.

"It's truly a miracle the Packers aren't trudging back to Lambeau Field to host the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday Night Football with a 0-2 record. And it's enough for LaFleur to start feeling some pressure."

Green Bay's issues in Week 2 also weren't a one-time occurrence. The Packers moved the ball in the season opener but committed two turnovers. They also had 12 penalties for 98 yards with just one takeaway in a 39-22 defeat to the Minnesota Vikings on September 13.

Winning in the NFL while not playing well is often the sign of a very good team. But the Packers have yet to prove this season they can play well. They also haven't put together a strong, complete 60-minute performance since early December last year.

For those reasons, alarm bells might still be going off in Green Bay despite the victory over the Jets.

The Packers needed 10 fourth-quarter points to force overtime during Week 2. Then, Green Bay stopped the Jets offense and kicked a field goal on its overtime drive to secure the win.

Quarterback Jordan Love might have saved LaFleur from really feeling the heat entering Week 3. Love completed 7 of 12 passes for 80 yards with a touchdown in the fourth quarterback and overtime combined.

The Packers were also able to overcome their sluggish offense and penalty mistakes because the Jets had even more penalty yardage. New York committed 13 fouls for 156 yards.
